chapters.subject: Mathematics – Algebra
chapters.textbookRef: Mathematics Part I – Standard X (Balbharati) • Chapter 1: Linear Equations in Two Variables
chapters.overview: Solve simultaneous linear equations using elimination, substitution, graphical method, Cramer's Rule (determinants), reducible equations, and word problems across Practice Sets 1.1 to 1.5.
keyPoints: General form of a linear equation in two variables: ax + by + c = 0 where a, b, c are real numbers and a ≠ 0, b ≠ 0 simultaneously.
2×2 Determinant value: |a b; c d| = ad − bc.
Cramer's Rule: For a₁x + b₁y = c₁ and a₂x + b₂y = c₂, D = |a₁ b₁; a₂ b₂|, Dₓ = |c₁ b₁; c₂ b₂|, Dᵧ = |a₁ c₁; a₂ c₂| ⇒ x = Dₓ/D, y = Dᵧ/D (D ≠ 0).
Equations like 2/x + 3/y = 15 are reduced to linear form by substituting 1/x = m and 1/y = n.
formulasAndRules: Determinant D = |a b; c d| = ad − bc
Cramer's Rule: x = Dₓ / D, y = Dᵧ / D (D ≠ 0)
Symmetric Sum-Difference Pattern: When coefficients of x and y interchange (e.g., 99x+101y=499, 101x+99y=501), first ADD and then SUBTRACT the two equations.

textbookExerciseSolutions.question: Solve: (1) 3a + 5b = 26; a + 5b = 22  (7) 99x + 101y = 499; 101x + 99y = 501
textbookExerciseSolutions.formulaExplained: Subtract equations with equal coefficients; for swapped coefficients, add first to get (x+y) and subtract to get (x−y).
textbookExerciseSolutions.stepByStepExplanation:
Sub-q (1): Subtract (a+5b=22) from (3a+5b=26) ⇒ 2a = 4 ⇒ a = 2. Substitute a=2: 2 + 5b = 22 ⇒ 5b = 20 ⇒ b = 4.
Sub-q (7): Add equations ⇒ 200x + 200y = 1000 ⇒ x + y = 5. Subtract eq(1) from eq(2) ⇒ 2x − 2y = 2 ⇒ x − y = 1. Adding gives 2x = 6 ⇒ x = 3, y = 2.

textbookExerciseSolutions.question: Solve using Cramer's Rule: (1) 3x − 4y = 10; 4x + 3y = 5  (4) 6x − 4y = −12; 8x − 3y = −2
textbookExerciseSolutions.formulaExplained: x = Dₓ/D, y = Dᵧ/D where D = a₁b₂ − a₂b₁.

textbookExerciseSolutions.question:
Q1: Two numbers differ by 3. The sum of twice the smaller number and thrice the greater number is 19. Find the numbers.
Q5: Two types of boxes A, B are placed in a truck of capacity 10 tons. When 150 boxes of A and 100 boxes of B are loaded, it weighs 10 tons; when 260 boxes of A are loaded, it still accommodates 40 boxes of B to reach 10 tons. Find weight of each box.
textbookExerciseSolutions.conceptUsed: Translating Word Conditions into Two Linear Equations
textbookExerciseSolutions.answer: Q1: Greater = 5, Smaller = 2  |  Q5: Box A = 30 kg, Box B = 55 kg
textbookExerciseSolutions.stepByStepExplanation:
Q1: Let greater = x, smaller = y. x − y = 3 and 3x + 2y = 19. Multiply first by 2: 2x − 2y = 6. Add: 5x = 25 ⇒ x = 5, y = 2.
Q5: 150x + 100y = 10000 ⇒ 3x + 2y = 200. Second: 260x + 40y = 10000 ⇒ 13x + 2y = 500. Subtract: 10x = 300 ⇒ x = 30 kg; 90 + 2y = 200 ⇒ y = 55 kg.

classNotebookExercises.modelAnswer: Adding gives 2x=10 ⇒ x=5, y=1; lines intersect at (5, 1).

classNotebookExercises.modelAnswer: When a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ (D=0), lines are either parallel (no solution) or coincident (infinitely many solutions).

revisionChecklist: Always rewrite equations in ax+by=c form before applying Cramer's Rule.

chapters.subject: Mathematics – Algebra
chapters.textbookRef: Mathematics Part I – Standard X (Balbharati) • Chapter 2: Quadratic Equations
chapters.overview: Solve quadratic equations by factorisation, completing the square, and formula method; analyse discriminant Δ = b²−4ac and Vieta's root relations across Practice Sets 2.1 to 2.6.
keyPoints: Nature of Roots (Δ = b² − 4ac): Δ = 0 ⇒ real & equal; Δ > 0 ⇒ real & unequal; Δ < 0 ⇒ not real.
If α, β are roots: α + β = −b/a and αβ = c/a; equation is x² − (α + β)x + αβ = 0.
formulasAndRules: Sum of roots α + β = −b/a | Product αβ = c/a

textbookExerciseSolutions.question: Solve by factorisation: (1) x² − 15x + 54 = 0  (6) 6x − 2/x = 1
textbookExerciseSolutions.formulaExplained: Multiply ax² + bx + c = 0 into factors (px+q)(rx+s) = 0.

textbookExerciseSolutions.question: Product of Pragati's age 2 years ago and 3 years hence is 84. Find her present age.
textbookExerciseSolutions.conceptUsed: Forming and Solving Quadratic Word Problem
textbookExerciseSolutions.stepByStepExplanation: Let present age = x. (x − 2)(x + 3) = 84 ⇒ x² + x − 6 = 84 ⇒ x² + x − 90 = 0 ⇒ (x + 10)(x − 9) = 0. Since age > 0, x = 9 years.

keyPoints: Common difference d = tₙ₊₁ − tₙ is constant in an A.P.
Sum of first n terms: Sₙ = (n/2)[2a + (n − 1)d] = (n/2)[t₁ + tₙ].

chapters.subject: Mathematics – Algebra
chapters.textbookRef: Mathematics Part I – Standard X (Balbharati) • Chapter 5: Probability
chapters.overview: Write exact sample spaces S for coins, dice, cards, and 2-digit numbers, identify events, and calculate classical probability P(A) = n(A)/n(S) across Practice Sets 5.1 to 5.4.
keyPoints: Sample Space S is the set of all possible outcomes; n(S) is its size.
Classical Probability: P(A) = n(A) / n(S), always 0 ≤ P(A) ≤ 1.
1 Coin: n(S)=2 | 2 Coins: n(S)=4 | 3 Coins: n(S)=8 | 1 Die: n(S)=6 | 2 Dice: n(S)=36 | Deck of Cards: n(S)=52.
formulasAndRules: 0 ≤ P(A) ≤ 1 (Probability can never be negative or > 1)

solvedExamples.prompt: Two dice are rolled simultaneously. Find the probability that the sum of digits on upper faces is at least 10.

textbookExerciseSolutions.question:
Q1: If two coins are tossed, find probability of (1) getting at least one head (2) getting no head.
Q4: A two-digit number is formed from digits 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 without repetition. Find probability that it is (1) even (2) divisible by 3 (3) greater than 50.
textbookExerciseSolutions.formulaExplained: Two-digit numbers cannot start with 0. Without repetition from 6 digits: 5 × 5 = 25 numbers.
textbookExerciseSolutions.stepByStepExplanation:
Q1: S = {HH, HT, TH, TT}, n(S)=4. At least 1 H = {HH,HT,TH} ⇒ P=3/4. No head = {TT} ⇒ P=1/4.
Q4: Total 2-digit numbers = 25 (tens digit 1..5, units 5 remaining). (1) Ending in 0: 5 nos; ending in 2 or 4: 4+4=8 ⇒ 13/25. (2) Multiples of 3 = 10 nos ⇒ 10/25 = 2/5. (3) Greater than 50: {51,52,53,54} = 4? Note 50 itself: {51,52,53,54} is 4, wait 50 is NOT > 50, so {51,52,53,54}=4/25; if ≥50 then 5/25=1/5. Wait textbook asks >50: exact count = {51,52,53,54} = 4 ⇒ 4/25!

classNotebookExercises.prompt: Define Sample Space and Event with one example.
classNotebookExercises.modelAnswer: Sample space S is the set of all possible outcomes (e.g. die roll S={1,2,3,4,5,6}); Event is any subset of S.
